html:
Milton Obote was the first prime minister of Uganda from independence in 1962 and later president, ruling twice, from 1962 to 1971 and from 1980 to 1985.

A northerner from Lango, he first allied with Buganda. In 1966 he suspended the constitution and sent the army under Idi Amin to storm the palace of the kabaka, Mutesa II, who fled into exile. In 1967 he abolished the kingdoms.

Amin overthrew him in 1971. He returned after the Uganda-Tanzania War and won a disputed election in 1980. His army's campaign against Museveni's guerrillas in the Bush War killed many civilians, and soldiers removed him again in 1985. He died in exile in Uganda's neighbour Zambia.
sum: Milton Obote was the first prime minister of Uganda from independence in 1962 and later president, ruling twice, from 1962 to 1971 and from 1980 to 1985.
